newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco finds new copper deposit -- minister.
newsitem.headline: Codelco finds new copper deposit -- minister.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco has discovered a new copper deposit in the northern Second Region, said Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky.
But Teplizky declined to give details of the discovery which was made by the corporation's Chuquicamata division.

"The private sector only gives information when a project is ready and approved by its board and shareholders, so let us study it (the deposit)," said Teplizky, quoted in newspaper El Mercurio. "We don't know the type, quantity or quality or other details of the reserve."
The paper quoted local officials as saying that Codelco has found traces of large copper deposits near the town of Calama.
Officials at Chuquicamata were not immediately available for comment.
Chuquicamata is Codelco's largest division with annual copper production of around 600,000 tonnes.
It lies an desert area especially rich in copper a stone's throw from the El Abra copper mine and Codelco's Radomiro Tomic pit which will begin production later this year.
